concepts.why: Patient has a positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, lymphocytopenia, and interstitial lung disease, which are all consistent with SLE.
Patient has symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal joints and interphalangeal joints, which is consistent with RA.
Patient has hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities on Chest CT, which are all consistent with ILD.
Patient has diffuse vasculopathy with fibrin thrombi in deep dermal vessels on skin biopsy, which is consistent with vasculitis.
Patient has a combination of features consistent with multiple connective tissue diseases, including SLE, RA, and ILD.
Patient has a positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, which is consistent with Sjögren's Syndrome.

rationales.F04: Symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal joints is more typical of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F08: Presence of anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies is highly suggestive of Sjögren's Syndrome and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
rationales.F09: Hilar lymphadenopathy and interstitial thickening on Chest CT are more typical of Interstitial Lung Disease and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
rationales.F10: Worsening interstitial lung disease on follow-up Chest CT is more typical of Interstitial Lung Disease.
rationales.F11: Restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity on pulmonary function tests is more typical of Interstitial Lung Disease.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including symmetric joint swelling, interstitial lung disease, and positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, are consistent with Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, which explains the combination of features from multiple autoimmune diseases.
